subject: Pharos Health: sudden p99 latency spike and throughput drop — prefetch/KV interference
messages:
From: Oliver King <oliver.king@pharoshealth.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>
Cc: Aisha Patel <aisha.patel@pharoshealth.com>
Date: Sun, 5 May 2029 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: URGENT: 9:00am PST spike — p99 latency up, errors increasing

Vivek,

We hit a pretty disruptive event starting ~08:45 PST — our service is seeing p50 ~120ms (normal) but p99 jumped to ~2.1s and error rate across calls to the Redwood endpoint is ~3.7%. Throughput to the endpoint is down ~40% compared to baseline. The SREs have attached traces and a log bundle (pharos_kv_logs_20290505.tar.gz) — they show a ton of cache eviction churn and a lot of repeated prefixes in the hotkey list.

This is impacting our triage flow for urgent care. Can you reset anything on your side that will get us back to normal while we collect more data? We need a mitigation ASAP — can we temporarily disable any prefetching behaviors or move us to a higher-priority lane?

I'm copying our SRE on the logs. Please let me know the ETA for any fix.

Thanks,
Oliver King
Head of Platform
Pharos Health

Attachments: pharos_kv_logs_20290505.tar.gz
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, jonas_weber@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai, grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
Cc: Oliver King <oliver.king@pharoshealth.com>
Date: Sun, 5 May 2029 09:24:30 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: URGENT: 9:00am PST spike — p99 latency up, errors increasing

Folks — forwarding Pharos' escalation. Key points from their SRE bundle:
- p99 latency ~2.1s; error rate ~3.7%; throughput -40%
- logs show aggressive prefetch activity and repeated KV evictions for tenant "pharos" leading to hot-key churn
- prefetch depth + aggressive batch coalescing seems to be thrashing their KV slab

Suggested immediate mitigations (please weigh in):
1) Temporarily disable prefetching for tenant pharos (fast rollback)
2) Increase per-tenant KV slab by 2x for the tenant (risk: memory pressure elsewhere)
3) Lower prefetch depth and reduce batch lane concurrency for tenant until we've confirmed behavior
4) If needed, route Pharos to dedicated priority lane (30min) while we monitor

Can Marissa/Jonas own a quick test of disabling prefetch for the tenant? Laura, can you prepare an exec-facing note and confirm whether we should offer credits if SLA breached? Oliver — we'll need to schedule a 30m sync once we have a short mitigation plan. Attaching our internal MOP for prefetch (MOP-prefetch-playbook-v1.pdf).

— Vivek
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>, Oliver King <oliver.king@pharoshealth.com>
Date: Sun, 5 May 2029 09:38:12 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: URGENT: 9:00am PST spike — p99 latency up, errors increasing

Quick update from ops triage:
- I kicked a safe toggle to disable tenant-level prefetch. Observed initial improvement in p99 (~+40% improvement within 90s) but there are residual evictions as the heap stabilizes.
- We also reduced per-tenant batch-concurrency from 16 -> 6 for the pharos tenant; this reduced batching-induced HOL blocking on affected hosts.

Immediate ask: Jonas — can you push a short-lived KV slab bump (tenant annotation) to 2x for pharos on the affected cluster (cluster-a)? It should be a metadata change and should avoid rolling infra. If memory spikes, we'll revert.

Oliver — attaching a short heapshot and early p99 charts. We'll watch for recurrence; if it reappears we'll consider auto-fallback to a compatible model variant with lower batch pressure.

Marissa

Attachments: heapshot-2029-05-05.txt
From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>, Oliver King <oliver.king@pharoshealth.com>
Date: Sun, 5 May 2029 10:05:47 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: URGENT: 9:00am PST spike — p99 latency up, errors increasing

Action taken:
- Applied tenant annotation pharos.kv.slab.multiplier=2.0 on cluster-a (no service restart). Memory usage increased but within headroom.
- Prefetch disabled for tenant pharos at 09:40 PST
- Batch lane concurrency patched (6) and hot-key detector thresholds lowered to avoid aggressive prefetching for repeated prefixes

Early results: p99 down to ~650ms, error rate down to ~0.6%, throughput recovering to ~85% baseline. We'll keep these temporary flags for 60 minutes and reassess.

Next steps:
- Execute deeper post-mortem: collect KV eviction timelines, prefetch/req traces and run a synthetic load to validate patch
- If patch proves stable, schedule a configuration change in the upcoming config window and bake it into the tenant-profile recommendations

Will prepare a short exec summary for Laura.

Jonas
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>, Oliver King <oliver.king@pharoshealth.com>
Date: Sun, 5 May 2029 17:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Exec sync scheduled: Pharos incident and remediation recap

Team,

Thanks for the quick response and for stabilizing Pharos' traffic. I'm scheduling a 30-minute exec sync at 18:15 PST today with Pharos leadership to cover what happened, what we did, and next steps (we should have initial post-mortem bullets by then):
- Timeline of spike and mitigation actions
- Temporary config changes (prefetch off, kv slab x2, batch-concurrency lowered)
- Short-term monitoring plan and rollback criteria
- Proposed permanent fixes (adaptive prefetch thresholds, tenant-aware slab sizing, auto-fallback lanes)

Oliver — we will share the post-mortem and baked config proposal. We'll also propose a one-time service credit if the final SLA review shows customer impact beyond thresholds.

Please confirm availability for the 18:15 PST call and attach any additional notes you want included in the exec deck.

Laura Bennett
VP, Customer Success
Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced: MOP-prefetch-playbook-v1.pdf
